newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends higher amid fund short covering.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends higher amid fund short covering.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures closed firmer and near the day's highs amid short-covering by the funds, market sources said.
The most-active July contract ended 1.05 cents higher at 73.49 cents per lb, having ranged from 73.70 to 73.00 cents, where support was pegged. Spot May closed up 1.23 cents at 71.88 cents.
Volume was estimated at a moderate 10,000 lots compared with Thursday's official 13,115 lots.

"It looks like the worst is behind us," Sharon Johnson, an analyst with Frank Schneider and Co Inc, said. "We weathered the storm of getting May liquidated and now the focus of the market will be liquidating spec shorts."

She said today's gains signaled the beginning of a short-covering rally, and pegged resistance between 74.00 and 76.50 cents per lb basis July. A decertification of stocks in the next two weeks, she said, "could add fuel to the rally."
Certificated stocks were unchanged from the previous session as of April 24, but remained high at 220,870 bales.

Carl Anderson, a marketing specialist with Texas A&M University, said that while today's gains were motivated by technicals, talk of lower-than-expected yields in Argentina could have provided some support to old crop futures.
The cool wet weather that has delayed planting in South Texas may be propping up new crop futures, he said.

"Obviously, it is too early to have any firm estimates but I'm hearing that acreage could be 100,000 or less," Anderson said, adding that planted area generally totals 200,000 to 250,000 acres in South Texas.
Open interest in May stood at 1,013 lots, down 1,752 lots as of early Thursday. Interest in July rose 1,351 lots to 41,930 lots.
